title: Card Advisory
summary: Use a Card Advisory to show one score with a sentence on what it means and, if it helps, one next step.

anatomy.title: A score, its reading, and a nudge
anatomy.description: A bold title and one sentence sit beside a small ring that shows the score out of 100. An inline nudge below gives one reason to act and one button.

configuration.title: Brand and status colours
configuration.description: AppearanceBrand colours the ring, the nudge, and its button: Storybook uses Neutral, and the package defaults to Primary. For a score that’s good or bad, set Semantic Intent to System and pick AppearanceSystem. The card itself stays white. Three slots, titleEndSlot, progressSlot, and nudgeSlot, replace the info icon, the ring, and the nudge with your own components.

sizing.title: Always 360 px wide
sizing.description: The card is 360 px wide, set by a token that no mode changes, and as tall as its content: it doesn’t stretch or shrink with its host. The ring is 60 px with 16 px before it, and the nudge sits 16 px below. It has no padding or corners: it’s a white section for a white screen.

content.title: Name it, read it, act on it
content.description: Keep the title to one or two words: it’s cut to one line. Say what the score means in one sentence, give the nudge one reason to act, and label its button with a verb; the default label is “Button”. Set accessibilityLabel to the score in words, such as “Spending score 70”, because the default reads out every line, the nudge included.

sources.title: Use the public Card Advisory contract
sources.description: The guide compares the Figma component with the installed package and its Storybook stories.
blocks: Installed jfs-components is 0.1.78 (16 October build) from the team’s private package repository. Figma’s Card / Advisory is one 360 × 136 component with a Title property; its nudge is the retired Nudge with a purple sparkle and no close button, a mix no single mode reproduces, so this page follows Storybook’s Neutral. The card passes no onClose, so since the #271 fix its nudge shows no Close button. The title is cut to one line and sits on a 32 px line (26 in Figma). The card stays white in every mode. Its default spoken name reads the title, description, score, and nudge text, even when the nudge is hidden. The published Storybook still shows the old page and the older nudge.
